title: Sitting in King Oliver's room: his stories of Louis and the breaks
summary: Oliver used a straight mute and told Phillips how he and Louis Armstrong played simultaneous breaks on Tiger Rag in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Now, to go on with King Oliver again. You were talking about he actually at one time took you up in his room...?
I used to go up in his room all the time.

So if you could tell us anything about... You say, going up in his room all the time, and he taught you some shortcuts. Any kind of mutes that you saw him using? Anything you'd say would be interesting.
No, he just had a straight mute that he used. He used that mute on a lot of solos he played.
What was that like, going up in his room?
Oh, we used to come into his room and we'd sit down and talk. He'd tell me about he and Louis used to make breaks together and all that. They broke up Chicago on that, you know.

Right, on like "Tiger Rag." They'd play together. King said they wouldn't rehearse it, wouldn't rehearse nothing. They'd just play it. Til Louis said, "All right, what if we start here?" Now, don't you forget it." Because wasn't gonna forget nothin'! He said Louis had the best memory for playing things, you know. He said they'd get it, but they'd make it. They'd come on down when they'd get that break.

Because another guy told me I should hear that way out in North Dakota. A band named the Butterfly Band. They were playing around Chicago. So I told him... He asked me I'd heard it, and I said "No." I'd never seen Louis then. Not then. I was with Bronson then.
So he was talking about the old days with Louis.

Talkin' about Louis and King in Chicago. Everybody used to come out and tell us. They'd say, "Man, you ought to go to Chicago and hear King Oliver and Louis Armstrong." That was when Louis was with King.
